title: Attorney General of South Carolina

context.text: Four-term Attorney General Alan Wilson, a Republican, is running for governor, so the seat is open. David Stumbo won the Republican nomination in the June 23, 2026 runoff over Stephen Goldfinch; Richard Hricik was unopposed in the Democratic primary.

candidates.name: David Stumbo
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 23, 2026 Republican primary runoff over Stephen Goldfinch.
candidates.currentRole: Solicitor, South Carolina's 8th Judicial Circuit (fourth term)

summary.text: David Stumbo is the Republican nominee. He is in his fourth term as solicitor (district attorney) for the 8th Judicial Circuit, covering four Upstate counties, and previously worked in the Attorney General's office prosecuting internet crimes against children. He centers his campaign on his prosecution experience, and proposes regional attorney general's offices around the state.

background.text: Law degree from the University of South Carolina School of Law and a bachelor's degree from Toccoa Falls College.

Served in the South Carolina Attorney General's Office, prosecuting internet crimes against children cases and supervising the state grand jury; earlier an assistant solicitor in the 11th Judicial Circuit.
Elected solicitor of the 8th Judicial Circuit; now serving a fourth term.

priorities.text: Public safety and rule-of-law enforcement: strengthen partnerships with local law enforcement and prosecutors and protect crime victims.
Defend constitutional liberties, "including religious liberty and parental rights," and challenge what he calls unlawful government overreach.
Expand investigations into internet crimes against children and establish regional attorney general's offices across the state.

statements.quote: the sanctity of life of the unborn, religious liberty, and parental rights must be protected
statements.context: On his campaign website's priorities section

record.text: Has served as elected solicitor of South Carolina's 8th Judicial Circuit through four terms, prosecuting criminal cases for four Upstate counties.

candidates.name: Richard Hricik
candidates.ballotNote: Unopposed in the June 9, 2026 Democratic primary, which was canceled.

summary.text: Richard Hricik is the Democratic nominee. A Charleston-area attorney with more than 30 years of civil litigation experience, including before the U.S. Supreme Court, and a former accountant, he runs what he calls a no-donation campaign and focuses on consumer protection, property rights and making the office more accessible to the public.

background.text: Law degree from William & Mary Law School and an accounting degree from Cleveland State University; former accountant.

More than 30 years as an attorney representing clients against corporations in state and federal courts; teaches criminal justice and constitutional law at William & Mary Law School and the Charleston School of Law.

priorities.text: Consumer protection against debt collectors, scammers, insurers and businesses, and protecting land and water from polluters and large projects.
Accept no campaign donations so that, in his words, no favors are owed.
Make the office answer calls and investigate wrongdoing; pay attention to data centers and large development projects.

researchNotes: Slate: the State Election Commission's candidate/sample-ballot tools (vrems.scvotes.sc.gov) are interactive and could not be read; the two-candidate slate rests on Ballotpedia, WIS-TV (Oct 14, 2026), the Greenville News (Oct 14, 2026) and the USA TODAY Network candidate guide. No third-party or independent AG candidate was found. Neither candidate has positions on the fixed issue statements beyond Stumbo's single abortion-related sentence; no direct statements on guns, immigration or other listed issues were found. Stumbo's solicitor-office casework was not reviewed case by case.
